title: St Joseph's Zeppole with Vanilla Cream and Cherries
summary: Baked choux rosettes filled with lemon-scented vanilla pastry cream and topped with amarena cherries.
equipment: stand mixer with paddle (or hand mixer)
2 piping bags, one with a 1.5 cm open star nozzle and one with a 1 cm star nozzle
2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
amarena (wild sour) cherries in syrup, drained

steps.title: Make the cream
steps.text: Heat the milk until small bubbles appear at the edge. Whisk the sugar and cornflour in a bowl, then whisk in the yolks and lemon zest until pale. Whisk in half the hot milk, pour it all back into the pan and whisk over medium heat until thick and bubbling in the middle; keep whisking for 1 min more (about 85 °C). Off the heat whisk in the vanilla and butter, sieve into a bowl, press cling film onto the surface and chill for at least 2 h.

steps.title: Cook the choux
steps.text: Bring the water, milk, butter, sugar and salt to the boil in the second pan. Off the heat add the flour in one go and beat until smooth, then stir over medium heat for 2 min until a thin film forms on the base.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Beat the paste in the mixer bowl for 2 min to cool it. Add the eggs in four goes, beating well each time, until the paste is shiny and drops from the paddle in a thick V.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: Using the 1.5 cm nozzle, pipe 12 rosettes of about 7 cm onto the trays, two coils each with a little hollow in the middle, leaving 4 cm between them.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 20 min, then turn the oven down to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and bake 12-15 min more, until deep golden, crisp and light, with no damp patches in the ridges. Pierce the side of each to let out steam and cool on the rack.

steps.title: Fill and top
steps.text: Whisk the cold cream until smooth, spoon it into the second piping bag and pipe a generous swirl into the centre of each zeppola. Top each with a cherry and serve within 2 h.

tips: The most common mistake is opening the oven in the first 20 min; the choux collapses and never crisps.
Bake until properly deep golden; pale choux goes soft under the cream.
Make the cream a day ahead if you like; whisk it smooth before piping.
Check the cherry label: choose amarena cherries in syrup without alcohol.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Unfilled choux keeps in an airtight tin for 1 day (re-crisp at 180 °C for 5 min). Filled zeppole are best within 2 h; keep in the fridge.
